---
title: "Quantum Error Correction — Review"
---


# Why correct errors?

::: {.callout-warning title="Core problem"}
Qubits are fragile → interactions with the environment → inevitable errors.
Classical computers are error-free. **Not the quantum ones.**
:::

**Two motivations:**

- **Short term**: hybrid algorithms require correction to be efficient
- **Long term**: proving asymptotic quantum superiority (Quantum Advantage)

---

# Common errors — Binary Symmetric Channel (BSC)

**Model:** each bit is flipped with probability $p_e$, independently.

| Transition | Probability |
|:---:|:---:|
| $0 \to 0$ or $1 \to 1$ | $1 - p_e$ |
| $0 \to 1$ or $1 \to 0$ | $p_e$ |

::: {.callout-note title="Convention"}
We assume $p_e \leq 0{,}5$ without loss of generality. If $p_e = 0{,}5$ → channel unusable.
:::

---

# Classic 3-bit repeat code

**Encoding:** $0 \to 000$, $\quad 1 \to 111$

**Decoding:** majority vote

**Residual error probability:**

$$p_e' = 3p_e^2(1-p_e) + p_e^3$$

::: {.callout-note title="To remember"}
For $p_e < 0{,}5$: $p_e' < p_e$ → error removed at $\mathcal{O}(p_e^2)$
:::

---

# Obstacles to QEC (Quantum Error Correction)

| # | Obstacle | Nature |
|:---:|:---|:---|
| 1 | **No-Cloning**: cannot copy $|\psi\rangle$ | No direct repetition |
| 2 | **Destructive measure**: any measure collapses the superposition | No reading without destruction |
| 3 | **Continuing errors**: $\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle \to (\alpha+\epsilon_0)|0\rangle+(\beta+\epsilon_1)|1\rangle$ | Continuum of errors to be corrected |

::: {.callout-tip title="Good news"}
Each of these obstacles has a solution → quantum error correction is **possible**.
:::

---

# Solutions to the 3 obstacles

| Obstacle | Solution |
|:---|:---|
| Non-cloning | **Tangle** (entanglement) in place of the copy |
| Destructive measure | **Parity measurements** (parity-check): reveal the error, not the state |
| Continuous errors | The correction **digitalizes** the errors → automatic discretization |

---

# Three-Qubit Bit-Flip Code

**Encoding:**

$$\alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle \;\longrightarrow\; \alpha|000\rangle + \beta|111\rangle$$

**Circuit:** 2 CNOT gates (logic qubit controls two ancillas $|0\rangle$)

**Detection:** 2 ancilla qubits + parity measurements comparing qubits two by two

| Bit-flip | $M_1$ | $M_2$ | Correction |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| None | $0$ | $0$ | $I \otimes I \otimes I$ |
| Qubit 1 | $1$ | $0$ | $X \otimes I \otimes I$ |
| Qubit 2 | $1$ | $1$ | $I \otimes X \otimes I$ |
| Qubit 3 | $0$ | $1$ | $I \otimes I \otimes X$ |

::: {.callout-note title="Key"}
The $M_1$, $M_2$ measurements reveal **nothing** about $\alpha$, $\beta$ → preserved quantum state.
:::

---

# Phase-Flip Code on 3 qubits (Three-Qubit Phase-Flip Code)

**Phase error (Z):** $|+\rangle \leftrightarrow |-\rangle$ (invisible in the $\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle\}$ base)

**Encoding:** 2 CNOTs + Hadamard $H$ gates on each qubit

$$\alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle \;\longrightarrow\; \alpha|{+}{+}{+}\rangle + \beta|{-}{-}{-}\rangle$$

**Principle:** a phase-flip in $\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle\}$ = bit-flip in $\{|+\rangle,|-\rangle\}$ → same techniques

| Ph-flip | $M_1$ | $M_2$ | Correction |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| None | $0$ | $0$ | $I \otimes I \otimes I$ |
| Qubit 1 | $1$ | $0$ | $Z \otimes I \otimes I$ |
| Qubit 2 | $1$ | $1$ | $I \otimes Z \otimes I$ |
| Qubit 3 | $0$ | $1$ | $I \otimes I \otimes Z$ |

---

# Shor Code — 9 qubits

**Construction:** concatenation (concatenation) of the two previous codes

- **External** level (3 blocks) → protects against **phase-flips** ($Z$)
- **Internal** level (blocks of 3 qubits) → protects against **bit-flips** ($X$)

**Encoded logic states:**

$$|0_L\rangle = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\big(|000\rangle+|111\rangle\big)\big(|000\rangle+|111\rangle\big)\big(|000\rangle+|111\rangle\big)$$

$$|1_L\rangle = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\big(|000\rangle-|111\rangle\big)\big(|000\rangle-|111\rangle\big)\big(|000\rangle-|111\rangle\big)$$

**Capacity:** fixes **any** bit-flip, phase-flip or combination on **any** of the 9 qubits.

---

# Fixed general error — Digitization of Errors

**General error on 1 qubit:**

$$|0\rangle \to a|0\rangle + b|1\rangle, \quad |1\rangle \to c|0\rangle + d|1\rangle$$

**Decomposition** (with $k=\frac{a+d}{2}$, $l=\frac{b+c}{2}$, $m=\frac{a-d}{2}$, $n=\frac{b-c}{2}$):

| Term | Error | Operator |
|:---:|:---|:---:|
| $k$ | No errors | $I$ |
| $l$ | Bit-flip | $X$ |
| $m$ | Phase-flip | $Z$ |
| $n$ | Bit-flip + Phase-flip | $XZ$ |

::: {.callout-warning title="Key phenomenon — Digitalization"}
Parity measurements **collapse** the continuous state on one of the 4 discrete cases.
→ Correcting a **continuum** of errors amounts to correcting 4 discrete types.
:::

---

# Depolarizing Channel

**Standard quantum noise model:**

| Event | Probability |
|:---|:---:|
| No errors | $1 - p_e$ |
| Bit-flip ($X$) | $p_e/3$ |
| Phase-flip ($Z$) | $p_e/3$ |
| Bit + Phase flip ($XZ$) | $p_e/3$ |

**Shor code on depolarizing channel:** error removed from $p_e$ to $\mathcal{O}(p_e^2)$

::: {.callout-note title="Template general"}
Under the assumption of independence of errors between qubits → any general noisy channel can be modeled as a depolarizing channel.
:::

---

# Hamming code (7.4) — Classic

**Parameters:** encodes 4 bits → 7 bits | rate $= 4/7 \approx 0{,}57$

**Detection:** $p = Hc \bmod 2$ syndrome

- $p = 000$ → no error
- $p \neq 000$ → position of the single error (among 7 possibilities)

**Fixes:** any single bit error

---

# CSS Codes (Calderbank-Shor-Steane)

**Principle:** construct quantum codes from compatible classical linear codes

- $X$ (bit-flip) errors corrected by classic code
- $Z$ (phase-flip) errors fixed by another classic code

## Steane Code — 7 qubits

**Built from:** Hamming code (7.4)

**Encode:** 1 logical qubit into **7 physical qubits** (vs. 9 for Shor)

**Capacity:** corrects any bit-flip and/or phase-flip on 1 single qubit

**Performance:** removes the error from $p_e$ to $\mathcal{O}(p_e^2)$ on the depolarizing channel

---

# Code comparison

| Code | Physical qubits | Logical Qubits | Rate | Correct |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|
| Bit repetition (classic) | 3 | 1 bit | $1/3$ | 1 bit-flip |
| Quantum bit-flip | 3 | 1 | $1/3$ | 1 bit-flip ($X$) |
| Quantum phase-flip | 3 | 1 | $1/3$ | 1 phase-flip ($Z$) |
| **Shor** | **9** | **1** | ****TK0__** | **$X$, $Z$, $XZ$ on 1 qubit** |
| **Steane (CSS)** | **7** | **1** | ****TK0__** | **$X$, $Z$, $XZ$ on 1 qubit** |

---

# Summary — Critical points

::: {.callout-warning title="Frequent pitfalls"}

- Encoding $\alpha|000\rangle + \beta|111\rangle$ **is not** 3 copies of $\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle$ → it is **entangled** state
- Parity measurements do **not** measure $\alpha$ or $\beta$ → state is not destroyed
- Digitalization is not a postulate → it is a **consequence** of the collapse by measurement
- Shor's code fixes **any** error on 1 qubit, not just $X$ or $Z$ separately

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Key formula to remember"}
$$p_e' = 3p_e^2(1-p_e) + p_e^3 \approx \mathcal{O}(p_e^2) \quad \text{pour } p_e \ll 1$$
:::
